column1: # Nightly fuzz count budgets (G6). One row per calibrated target:
# measured_execs_10m is what the target reached in a 10-minute duration-mode
# nightly run on ubuntu-latest (nightly run 39570511158, 2026-10-21); it is the
# ceiling check_fuzz_policy.sh holds every budget under.
# budget_execs is 7 minutes at the rate the target actually sustained in COUNT
# mode (nightly run 40076940398, 2026-10-24: last "elapsed, execs" line per
# job). The first calibration, 80% of the duration-mode count, sent 12 of 39
# targets past their 15-minute job limit: count-mode throughput is lower.
# A count budget (-fuzztime <N>x) has no wall-clock deadline, so it avoids the
# Go fuzz engine's deadline race (golang/go#76901: a duration budget that runs
# out mid-worker reports "context deadline exceeded" as a failure).
# A target with no row falls back to FUZZ_NIGHTLY_FUZZTIME. check_fuzz_policy.sh
# refuses a row for an undiscovered target or a budget above its measurement.
